event.title: Senate Judiciary Committee Postpones Vote on Todd Blanche's Attorney General Nomination
event.canonical_title: Senate Judiciary Committee Postpones Vote on Todd Blanche's Attorney General Nomination
event.summary: The Senate Judiciary Committee has postponed a key vote on Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general, amid concerns from two Republican senators. The delay raises questions about Blanche's confirmation as President Trump's pick for the position, particularly in light of issues related to Trump's IRS lawsuit. The Department of Justice has expressed its willingness to work with the senators to advance the nomination.

The confirmation vote comes amid ongoing discussions regarding Trump's lawsuit against the IRS over his leaked tax returns.

event_overview.title: About DOJ Nomination
event_overview.subject: DOJ Nomination
event_overview.summary: This event is the Senate’s consideration of President Donald Trump’s nomination of Todd Blanche to be Attorney General of the United States, the Senate-confirmed head of the Department of Justice. The Senate Judiciary Committee conducts the initial hearing and committee review; its action determines whether the nomination is reported for consideration by the full Senate, which provides the required advice and consent.

facts.label: Nominee and office
facts.value: Todd Blanche was nominated to be Attorney General of the United States, replacing Pamela Bondi. At the time of the committee proceedings, he was serving as Acting Attorney General and as the 40th Deputy Attorney General.

facts.label: Legal framework
facts.value: Federal law provides that the President appoints the Attorney General with the advice and consent of the Senate; the Attorney General is the head of the Department of Justice.

facts.label: Senate process
facts.value: The Senate Judiciary Committee has jurisdiction to consider executive nominations including senior Department of Justice positions, while the full Senate ultimately acts on the nomination.

facts.label: Committee hearings
facts.value: The committee held Blanche’s nomination hearing on July 15, 2026, followed by a second day of testimony on July 16, in Room 216 of the Hart Senate Office Building in Washington, D.C.

facts.label: Department role
facts.value: The Attorney General leads the Department of Justice, represents the United States in legal matters, and provides legal advice and opinions to the President and executive-department heads when requested.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the late-July postponement and August 4 committee action on this nomination, not every hearing exchange, negotiation, or subsequent full-Senate step.

related_events.title: Trump's Settlement Fund Threat Complicates Attorney General Confirmation Talks
related_events.summary: Trump has threatened to advance a proposed $1.8 billion settlement fund if Senate Republicans do not confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general. This statement, made via Truth Social, has introduced new uncertainty into the ongoing discussions regarding Blanche's confirmation, particularly involving Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis.
